title: The BENQODHI Workshop
text:
What the workshop does
BENQODHI convenes experts in quantum computing, optimisation, AI, biology and health to define credible, open benchmarks for transparent comparison across quantum, hybrid, AI, and classical approaches.
The two days are structured around four themes:

Foundations & use cases (Day 1) — invited talks covering benchmarking practice and concrete use cases from bioinformatics, genomics and health.
Benchmark design (Day 2 morning) — parallel working tables turning Day 1’s exchanges into concrete candidate benchmark problems.
JRC quantum laboratories (Day 2 midday) — a guided visit.
European strategy (Day 2 afternoon) — a policy session connecting the technical work to European decisions on quantum and hybrid computing for health and biology.

See the program page for the detailed timing and the speakers page for who is contributing.

title: The BENQODHI Workshop
text:
Target outputs

Three focused candidate benchmark dossiers.
One shared framework note covering instances, baselines, metrics, resource accounting, reporting and repository needs.
A named owner for every follow-up.

title: The BENQODHI Workshop
text:
Invited speakers and institutional contributors
Professors and researchers from Sapienza University of Rome, Leiden University, IBM Research Europe (Zurich), ICREA and Universitat Pompeu Fabra, SISSA, PacBio, IRCCS Ospedale San Raffaele, Barcelona Supercomputing Centre, CINECA and the University of Cagliari.
Representatives from DG CNECT, DG SANTE, DG DEFIS and the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking are also invited to contribute.

title: Problems
text:
BENQODHI is building a set of candidate benchmark problems at the intersection of optimisation, life sciences and health. This page tracks the working-table themes for the Day 2 working session and the candidate problems proposed so far.
Candidates are welcome from anyone — see Contribute for how to propose one.

title: Problems
text:
Common template
Every candidate problem is described using the same structure, so proposals, working notes and finished problem pages all stay comparable:

Use case — the biological or clinical task, and why it matters
Formal problem — objective, decision variables, constraints
Instances — real, synthetic or generated; provenance, scale, format
Source of difficulty — why it is hard
Baselines — current methods and available implementations
Metrics — success measures, resource accounting
Ready vs. missing — honest gap analysis
Next action — one named person, one concrete step

title: Share an Idea
text:
Before the workshop, participants can leave short ideas to help shape the discussion at JRC Ispra. One idea is enough: a candidate benchmark problem, a suggestion for the working session, a panel question, or a practical note about datasets, metrics or baselines.
Ideas are collected as public GitHub Issues. Choose the closest type: candidate problem, session organisation, panel question, dataset/baseline/metric, or other.
If GitHub is inconvenient, send your idea by email: JRC-F7-CONFERENCES@ec.europa.eu

title: Share an Idea
text:
Example Ideas


Radiotherapy planning as a benchmark problem
Radiotherapy treatment planning is a concrete health optimization problem that could be discussed as a BENQODHI benchmark. Useful notes would include objectives, constraints, available instances, baselines and evaluation metrics.


Day 2 working-table structure
The Day 2 morning session could be organised around three provisional tables: bioinformatics, health problems, and machine learning or quantum/benchmark practice. Participants can suggest different tables, additional themes or a simpler format.


If your idea is a candidate benchmark problem, please mention:

what the biological or health use case is,
what needs to be optimized,
what data or instances might be available,
why the problem is hard or interesting,
which baselines or metrics could be useful.

Partial sketches are welcome.

title: BENQODHI
text:
JRC exploratory activity





Can quantum computing make a measurable difference on optimization problems that matter in life sciences? BENQODHI brings together quantum computing, optimisation, AI, biology and health experts to define open benchmarks for fair comparison across classical, AI-based, hybrid and quantum approaches.

Workshop Contribute






10-11 Sept 2026
JRC Ispra, Italy


Open benchmarks
Reusable problem instances


Comparable evidence
Baselines, metrics, resources
BENQODHI is a European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC) exploratory activity. It is shaped around a simple question: which health and biology optimization problems are specific, measurable and useful enough to become shared benchmarks?
Organised by JRC.F.7 within the BENQODHI exploratory activity granted by JRC.S.4. Organisers: Indaco Biazzo · Antonio Puertas Gallardo · Tobias Wiesenthal. Workshop coordination and logistics: Ilse Verspreet.
